GDACS's earthquake report (event 1554552) for this M6.8 Kumamoto earthquake assesses an Orange alert ("this earthquake can have a medium humanitarian impact based on the magnitude and the affected population and their vulnerability"), with an exposed population of about 1.2 million people at MMI VII or greater. No confirmed casualty figure is given.

The Minami-Kyushu Expressway (Yatsushiro-Tamura, damaged section) remains closed to general traffic, with reopening still targeted for late August; the Kyushu Shinkansen (Kumamoto-Shin-Minamata) and two local rail lines remain suspended.

claims.text: FDMA Report No. 54 (16 August 2026, 10:00 JST): the national death toll remains 39 and injured/missing figures are unchanged (397 injured nationally, 27 missing); housing damage assessments continued to rise between Report No. 51 (13 Aug) and No. 54 (16 Aug) -- total collapse 1,274 to 1,287 units, half collapse 1,046 to 1,185 units, and total damaged-housing units 11,796 to 13,952 -- reflecting ongoing survey completion. Evacuation instructions remain in force for 3 municipalities (103,922 households / 219,027 people). As of 14 August 17:00, further prefectural Emergency Fire Response Team reinforcements (from Fukuoka, Saga, Oita, Miyazaki and Kagoshima) withdrew; Kumamoto Prefecture's disaster response headquarters, established 28 July, remains active.

USGS's PAGER population-exposure estimate for this earthquake found about 1,422,182 people exposed to MMI VII (Very Strong) shaking or greater and about 8,057,091 additional people exposed to MMI V (Moderate) shaking, almost entirely within Japan (a small population of about 65 people in South Korea was exposed to MMI III, weak, shaking).

USGS PAGER's loss-model data, updated 29 July 2026, records a maximum shaking intensity of MMI IX, a fatality alert level of Orange (gvalue 1.77, up from Yellow) and an economic alert level of Red (gvalue 2.28). Aggregated population exposure at MMI VII or greater is about 1,236,912 (374,783 at MMI VII + 635,782 at MMI VIII + 226,347 at MMI IX). PAGER's empirical loss model estimates 724 total fatalities (0 in South Korea) and $12,724,898,845 in economic losses; PAGER's semi-empirical structural model separately estimates 234 fatalities. These are automated probabilistic model outputs, not confirmed casualty or damage figures.

description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck southern Kumamoto Prefecture, Kyushu, Japan, on 28 July 2026 at 07:27 UTC (16:27 local time), 5 km east of Uto City, at a depth of about 10 km. USGS's PAGER system initially assessed an overall Red alert level (economic-loss alert Red, fatality alert Yellow) with a maximum estimated shaking intensity of MMI VIII (Severe); a PAGER loss-model update as of 29 July 2026 raised the maximum estimated shaking to MMI IX (Violent) and upgraded the fatality alert from Yellow to Orange, with the economic alert remaining Red — PAGER's probabilistic loss models now estimate roughly 724 fatalities (empirical model) or 234 fatalities (semi-empirical structural model) and about $12.7 billion in economic losses. About 1.24 million people were exposed to MMI VII (Very Strong) shaking or greater, almost entirely within Japan. As of 3 August 2026, these remain PAGER's automated probabilistic estimates — no allowlisted authoritative source has yet published confirmed casualty or damage figures, though non-allowlisted international media report a Japanese-government-confirmed death toll that had risen into the mid-30s by 1 August. Re-checked 5 August 2026: USGS's event page and feed for us6000tgb9 still show no PAGER product update since 29 July 2026; no allowlisted source has published confirmed casualty or damage figures. Re-checked 8 August 2026: USGS's PAGER product for this event is unchanged — magnitude 6.8, Red alert, maximum MMI 9, with the same loss-model figures already cited; the event feed's top-level 'updated' timestamp advanced (routine shakemap/DYFI reprocessing) but the PAGER casualty/economic-loss estimates did not change. Re-checked 9 August 2026: a GDACS earthquake report (event 1554552) now exists for this event, assessing an Orange alert with about 1.2 million people exposed to MMI VII+ shaking. USGS's PAGER product remains unchanged since 29 July 2026 (Red alert, max MMI 9, modeled fatality estimates of 724/234 — not confirmed figures). No allowlisted source has yet published a confirmed casualty or damage figure. Re-checked 10 August 2026: USGS's PAGER product is unchanged (Red alert, max MMI 9.24); the event page additionally shows a Red liquefaction hazard alert (~240,000 people exposed) and an Orange landslide hazard alert (~2,800 people exposed). No allowlisted source has published a confirmed casualty or damage figure. Re-checked 11 August 2026: USGS's PAGER product (fatality alert Orange, economic alert Red) and GDACS's earthquake report both remain unchanged from the prior check; no allowlisted source has yet published a confirmed casualty or damage figure for this earthquake. Re-checked 12 August 2026: prior checks of this record were limited to USGS/GDACS/ReliefWeb, none of which publish a confirmed casualty figure for a domestic Japanese earthquake. Direct fetch of Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency (FDMA) numbered situation-report series -- the national government's own official casualty and damage reporting for this earthquake -- found a confirmed toll of 39 deaths (Report No. 50, 12 August 2026, 13:00 JST), essentially unchanged since around Report No. 34 (8 August 2026), plus 1,252 fully destroyed and 1,046 half-destroyed buildings (11,240 total damaged). Evacuation instructions remain in effect for 3 municipalities (103,922 households / 219,027 people). Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) reports the Kyushu Expressway has reopened to emergency vehicles system-wide, but water outages persist in 15 municipalities across 4 prefectures as of 11 August 2026. USGS's PAGER product and GDACS's report remain unchanged from prior checks (automated model estimates, not confirmed figures). FDMA Report No. 51 (13 August 2026) shows the confirmed death toll unchanged at 39 while building-damage totals continue to rise (1,274 fully destroyed, ~11,796 total damaged); MLIT's Report No. 39 shows water outages sharply reduced from a peak of ~108,100 households to ~28,400 households in 3 municipalities, with full restoration targeted by end of August, while the Kyushu Shinkansen and two rail lines remain suspended and the expressway remains closed to general traffic. Re-checked 14 August 2026: FDMA Report No. 52 (14 August 2026) confirms the death toll unchanged at 39, while total damaged buildings rose to 12,367 (up from ~11,796) as fully/half-destroyed counts continue to climb (1,275/1,088). MLIT Report No. 40 (same date) reports water outages further reduced to ~27,800 households and, as of 14 August 06:00, the Kyushu Expressway reopened to general vehicles system-wide for the first time since the quake (one section under alternating one-lane control), though the Minami-Kyushu Expressway and Kyushu Shinkansen remain closed/suspended. Re-checked 15 August 2026: FDMA Report No. 53 (15 August 2026, 10:00 JST) confirms the death toll unchanged at 39, while total damaged buildings rose to 13,491 (up from 12,367; 1,283 fully destroyed, up from 1,275; 1,162 half destroyed, up from 1,088). MLIT Report No. 41 (same date) reports water outages further reduced to about 27,400 households in three Kumamoto municipalities (of which ~16,500 already have flow restored under a conservation request), and confirms the Kyushu Expressway is now fully open to general vehicles system-wide (one section under alternating one-lane control near Kawada bridge), while the Minami-Kyushu Expressway and Kyushu Shinkansen remain closed/suspended, with general-vehicle reopening of the expressway's closed section still targeted for late August. Re-checked 16 August 2026: FDMA Report No. 54 (16 August, 10:00 JST) keeps the death toll steady at 39, with housing-damage assessments continuing to rise (total damaged-housing units up from 11,796 to 13,952 between 13 and 16 August) as surveys are completed; evacuation instructions covering ~219,000 people remain in force. National emergency fire-response reinforcements are progressively withdrawing, but Kumamoto Prefecture's disaster headquarters remains formally active and JMA continues to warn of elevated aftershock risk for at least another month.
